title: Number of Pairs of Strings With Concatenation Equal to Target
summary: Given an array of digit strings and a target digit string, count the number of unique index pairs (i, j) where i does not equal j, such that the concatenation of the digit strings at these indices matches the target.
statement: Given an array of digit strings and a target digit string, count the number of unique index pairs (i, j) where i does not equal j, such that the concatenation of the digit strings at these indices matches the target.
constraints: nums has 2 through 100 digit strings and target is a nonempty digit string.
Count ordered index pairs i!=j for which nums[i]+nums[j] equals target.
Equal strings at different indices remain distinct choices.
hints: For a current string, it may be either the first or second member of a pair with an earlier string.
Maintain frequencies of earlier strings and query the exact complementary prefix or suffix when target matches.
If target starts with x query remaining suffix; if target ends with x query remaining prefix; then record x.
Each ordered pair is counted when its later index arrives, in the orientation where that value appears; exact splitting guarantees concatenation equality.
editorial: Each ordered pair is counted when its later index arrives, in the orientation where that value appears; exact splitting guarantees concatenation equality.

tests.explanation: The ordered compatible choices produce four index pairs.
